scope: Different-author source-only hammer of M2006. It ran the official test and an independent attack harness under CPython 3.6 and 3.12, inspected source/contract/seals, and used only synthetic TemporaryDirectory archives and namespaces. The production remote archive, canonical shard/payload namespaces, merge, reducer, GPU, and EDA were not opened or executed.

p1.finding: M2006 reuses M2003._copy_result_tree. A crash after copytree creates <result>.m2003_import_work but before rename leaves that work directory. On manual_resume_from_verified_plan, _install_or_compare_remote does not recognize or quarantine this import-work namespace; the second _copy_result_tree call rejects it as already existing. The independent synthetic attack reproduced first failure, orphan persistence, and second failure.
p1.impact: The sole authorized recovery path can be permanently stranded after a normal mid-copy interruption even though the sealed verified plan and immutable staging tree remain valid. This does not close M2004's required recoverable import transaction.
p1.required_repair: An additive successor must explicitly model per-result import work. On resume, verify/quarantine a pre-existing import-work tree without deleting or overwriting it, then restart into a fresh O_EXCL work name or safely complete a fully sealed tree. Add interruptions before copy, mid-copy, after seal, and before publish as permanent regressions.

p1.finding: _publish_verified_plan checks PLAN absence, builds and seals PLAN.work, then calls Path.rename(PLAN). POSIX rename can replace an empty target directory that appears between the check and rename. The independent verify-hook race created that target after sealing and observed its inode replaced. The same check-then-rename family is used by process/result/failure publication and inherited per-shard result publication.
p1.impact: The implementation claims no overwrite but canonical publication is not no-replace atomic. A concurrent or interrupted namespace transition can be silently replaced, violating the explicit no-overwrite transaction boundary.
p1.required_repair: Use a no-replace publication primitive (renameat2 RENAME_NOREPLACE where available, or an atomic lock/link protocol with exact topology verification and fsync) for plan, process receipt, failure, final result, and imported result trees. Preserve collision evidence and add a raced-target regression.

p2.finding: _publish_result writes archive_open_count=0 whenever resumed=True, even though a sealed plan can only exist after the initial leg opened and extracted the one authorized archive. The correct campaign total is one; zero is only the resume-leg delta.
p2.disposition: Report cumulative campaign_archive_open_count=1 and a separate resume_archive_open_count=0, both checked by the result hammer.

p2.finding: classify_process_records validates cmdline_text but never requires cmdline_sha256 == SHA256(cmdline_text bytes) and does not enforce an exact process-record key set. A synthetic five-role record with an all-zero launcher cmdline hash is accepted.
p2.disposition: Validate exact process-record keys and text/hash consistency, and re-read all five PID/starttime identities after classification before publishing the live receipt.

single_next_action: Create an additively numbered successor that makes all canonical publication no-replace and makes partial imported-result work recoverable from the sealed plan; then obtain a fresh different-author source hammer before any process capture or release authoring.
